transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-28 15:00 UTC
Length: 47 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Links shared: pricing-sheet-v3.xlsx, redwood-security-report-v2.pdf, dpa-exception-matrix.xlsx, dev-vpc-instructions.md

Summary:
Quick procurement handoff focused on KMS pricing and DPA exceptions; technical team to run a brief latency benchmark in customer dev VPC; legal to confirm minimal redlines; follow-up pricing and security artifacts to be delivered within a week.

Topics: 
- Pricing breakdown: hosted vs dedicated, KMS/HSM overlay, egress and reserved commit examples
- DPA exceptions and data residency concerns (EU partial residency)
- KMS keying model: customer-managed keys (BYOK) vs Redwood-managed with HSM escrow
- Onboarding timeline and pilot acceptance criteria

Action items (high level): see action_items field above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan Park: ok hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is ethan from Redwood inference, i'm the AE on the account. we brought sofia and noah from solutions to cover security and the quick bench. how's everyone?
[00:08] Jared Mills: hey ethan, thanks. we're short on time so i'll try to keep it tight.
[00:12] Priya Desai: hi all, priya here, ciso. main thing for us is KMS and DPA exceptions — what we ship to legal.
[00:18] Ethan Park: great, quick agenda: pricing handoff, DPA/KMS model, pilot bench, next steps. sound good?
[00:22] Amelia Yuan: yes, legal will need the DPA matrix and the standard redlines.
[00:26] Sofia Alvarez: hi, sofia, security eng — i'll walk through the KMS and key management options then highlight our SOC2 scope and what we can share.
[00:31] Liam O'Connor: liam, cloud arch. we'll want the dev VPC bench to mirror our infra, especially egress and key wrapping latency.

[00:40] Ethan Park: cool. starting with pricing — i know procurement wants clarity on the KMS add-on and egress. we've sent a draft pricing-sheet-v3.xlsx earlier. quick run-through: hosted API does per-token pricing; you can enable customer-managed KMS for an add-on fee (flat monthly plus per-key operations). dedicated reserved pools have a monthly commit; burst capacity is billed separately. egress is charged above threshold.
[01:05] Jared Mills: can you be specific — for a 100k monthly token workload, with KMS? we're trying to model monthly cost.
[01:11] Ethan Park: sure, so in the sheet i've laid out three scenarios: 1) hosted + redwood KMS (no BYOK), 2) hosted + BYOK (customer key) where there's a $5k MOS fee + $0.02 per key op, 3) dedicated reserved with KMS overlay. i'll send a quick table after. the $5k is to cover HSM provisioning and key escrow if needed.
[01:30] Priya Desai: that $5k, is it per key or per tenant? also, what about the obligation to rotate keys on our side?
[01:36] Sofia Alvarez: it's per-tenant provisioning. rotation is supported on both sides — you can schedule rotation and we support envelope encryption. we don't retain plaintext keys.
[01:45] Amelia Yuan: legal will ask if we can require customer-only access to keys, i.e. no Redwood engineer access. is that supported?
[01:51] Sofia Alvarez: yes, with BYOK we configure key policies so Redwood cannot export or view private key material; access is logged to the audit trail. there's still meta-ops needed for incidents — we can discuss escalation paths where access is required under court order etc.
[02:04] Liam O'Connor: ok from an architecture side, how does KMS add latency on inference path? if wrapping/unwrapping happens per-request that's rough.
[02:12] Noah Reed: good question — we typically use KMS for key wrapping during bootstrapping and use ephemeral data keys in memory for the runtime; per-token ops don't hit KMS. so added latency is in the startup and rotation flows, not per inference. we benchmarked P95 cold-starts with BYOK at +120ms median in earlier tests but warm path is negligible.
[02:34] Priya Desai: that cold start number is close to what we care about. a few hundred ms is ok but we need to baseline.
[02:40] Ethan Park: that's why we offered to run a short benchmark in your dev VPC: run our serving runtime against a pinned checkpoint, measure P50/P95 and token cost, including a simulated rotation event. noah and liam will coordinate.
[02:52] Liam O'Connor: yes we'll open access. is there an agent or sidecar needed in our VPC?
[02:56] Noah Reed: no, it's a small runner we deploy as a short-lived pod — instructions in dev-vpc-instructions.md. we'll need an IAM role and a small subnet.
[03:06] Jared Mills: timeline? we can't have infra people tied up for weeks.
[03:09] Ethan Park: estimate is under a day of lift from your side, then an hour of run time for the bench. scheduling the run w/c 2026-06-08 per earlier note.
[03:18] Amelia Yuan: legal question about DPA: we have an EU residency constraint for a piece of data. can we carve that into the DPA or will Redwood insist on a full EU region support?
[03:27] Sofia Alvarez: we support region pinning for data-in-transit and rest; partial residency is possible by routing workloads to EU-only hosts and isolating logs — but we need the DPA exception matrix to capture the exact clauses.
[03:37] Amelia Yuan: also need to know retention of KV cache content — our privacy team is concerned about prefixes being cached.
[03:43] Sofia Alvarez: prefix/KV caching is stored encrypted, and can be configured to zero retention beyond session; we can offer a TTL of zero for sensitive models and also support per-route configs. we'll note that in the DPA doc.
[03:55] Priya Desai: are audit logs sufficient for our SOC2 team? we need immutable logs with exports.
[04:01] Sofia Alvarez: yes, we have audit logs export to your S3 or SIEM, and we support WORM-like retention policies. we'll point you to the redwood-security-report-v2.pdf which includes audit log details.
[04:12] Ethan Park: circling back to pricing: procurement asked if there's room for a short pilot/POC pricing that waives the KMS provisioning fee for a three-week pilot. i noted that for pilots we can often credit the MOS fee or apply a trial waiver; final approval sits with our finance team.
[04:27] Jared Mills: we'd need that formally in writing. otherwise legal won't sign.
[04:30] Ethan Park: understood — i'll mark that as requested and add to next_steps.
[04:35] Amelia Yuan: for legal redlines: our standard is to remove liability caps for data breaches and require breach notification in 48 hours. do you accept those?
[04:42] Ethan Park: our standard MSA has a liability cap but enterprise contracts can negotiate. i'll have legal weigh in after you provide the specific redlines.
[04:49] Amelia Yuan: okay i'll send the redlines.
[04:52] Sofia Alvarez: small technical note on backups: if you route backups to customer S3, that satisfies many of the data residency asks; we can also do on-prem backup if needed.
[05:00] Liam O'Connor: what about traffic egress — the cost model on the sheet assumes 5TB/month included; our spikes are heavier. what's the egress tier after that?
[05:08] Ethan Park: after included threshold egress is $0.09/GB tiered down as volume increases. we're open to negotiating tiers for reserved commitments.
[05:17] Jared Mills: procurement also needs billing cadence — monthly or quarterly?
[05:20] Ethan Park: by default monthly invoice; for enterprise we can do quarterly or annual commit with credit terms.
[05:26] Priya Desai: a quick compliance follow-up — do you offer a contract clause for customer-controlled encryption that prevents Redwood from decrypting telemetry for debugging?
[05:35] Sofia Alvarez: telemetry can be redacted upstream; debug-only telemetry requires explicit customer opt-in — boundaries will be written in the DPA/Annex.
[05:44] Noah Reed: also to add, our runtime collects aggregate perf metrics automatically but any PII is scrubbed; if you want strict separation we can route metrics to your own collector.
[05:53] Amelia Yuan: noted.
[05:56] Ethan Park: ok let's talk timeline: procurement wants an initial legal packet + updated pricing by next week, bench the week after, then a 30-day pilot. does that map?
[06:05] Jared Mills: yes but we'd like the pilot to include a rollback SLA and acceptance criteria.
[06:09] Sofia Alvarez: acceptance criteria we typically propose: P95 under agreed threshold, functional correctness for sample prompts, and no unauthorized key access. rollback policy is standard — we snapshot config and can revert; we'll put specifics in the runbook.
[06:20] Liam O'Connor: one more for infra — what are the minimum GPU sizes supported? we have A10s and occasional A100s.
[06:26] Noah Reed: our runtime supports broad choices; for quantitative match to cost/latency we can recommend instance families per workload. A10 will work for prototype but for production we usually recommend A100 or equivalent for throughput.
[06:36] Priya Desai: anything on location of logs for EU-only workloads?
[06:39] Sofia Alvarez: logs can be routed to EU-only S3 and we can disable cross-region replication by config.
[06:45] Ethan Park: ok we're at about 40 minutes — want to open to final Qs and capture decisions.
[06:50] Amelia Yuan: legal will need DPA exception matrix and the specific clause language for KMS controls.
[06:55] Ethan Park: will share those (Sofia to attach security report + matrix).
[06:58] Jared Mills: procurement needs the pricing sheet with a pilot waiver penciled in.
[07:02] Ethan Park: noted — i'll propose a pilot credit in the sheet.
[07:05] Liam O'Connor: i'll coordinate IAM access for the bench with noah, expect an email with steps.
[07:09] Noah Reed: yep, i'll send.
[07:12] Priya Desai: last one — can you confirm retention windows for KV cache and audit logs in writing?
[07:18] Sofia Alvarez: yes we'll list retention options in the DPA addendum: 0/7/30/90 day presets and customizable TTLs.
[07:25] Ethan Park: great. quick recap: 1) ethan sends updated pricing with pilot waiver option; 2) sofia sends security report + DPA matrix; 3) noah & liam run dev-vpc bench w/c 2026-06-08; 4) amelia sends legal redlines. action items reflected in notes.
[07:45] Jared Mills: that sums it up, thanks.
[07:48] Ethan Park: thanks all, we’ll follow up over email.
[07:50] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: speakers overlap occasionally; some technical terms transcribed imprecisely (e.g., MOS fee vs MOP), timestamps approximate.
